title: Funnel Cauchy slope = ||proj(g_n)||^2 instead of g_n . proj(g_n) (G4 y-iteration deadlock, round-d end game)
notes: Trace (HS83 tfip): y-iterations with d=0 because the tangential solver's Cauchy step is exactly 0: slope = g_n . proj(g_n) cancels to eps |g_n|^2 (|g_n| = 306, |proj g_n| = 2.9e-6) and is NEGATIVE (-1.9e-11 vs ||proj g_n||^2 = 8.7e-12), so alpha_c = 0, cg = 0. 3-line fix: slope = dot(r0, r0). Group multiplier_failure 3/13 (HS15, HS83, +1; rest become termination_missed 2, local_minimum 1, cycling 1); tfip medium union 166 -> 169; trip unchanged. Tiny tfip: +3 gained, 1 lost: HS86 tfip (solves at base 86ad709, real): now ends multiplier_solve_failure with f within 2e-6 of f*, stat 3.4e-7, compl 1.6e-6; the tangential radius collapses geometrically to 1e-149 with a_star = 0.3 steps rejected (rounding-level f-iteration rejections, no exit), i.e. a second end-game deadlock. subproblem/solver tests 415 passed. Falsified on the way: forcing the tangential step when v <= eps_v (infeasibility_dominates & v > eps_v) changes nothing (0/13). Gain/regression 3:1: waiver the user's call. Next: fix the radius-collapse in the funnel f-iteration at rounding level (HS86), then merge with this.

title: DUALC1/2/5/8 trip infeasible start: findings (normal step)
notes: Traced DUALC5 trip (n=8, 1 eq, 277 ineq): the normal step is ill-scaled, not capped by the radius: Cauchy alpha* = pi_v^2/||A d||^2 = 4e-9..1e-5 (||A|| ~ 1e4: the inequality rows dominate the least-squares normal step and the equality row, whose violation 0.92 is the whole v, is nearly invisible), CG hits its 50-iteration cap each call (n_cg = 50) and decreases v by only 1e-4..2e-4 per step (dm_v ~ 2e-4 on v = 0.92); then nu climbs to 6e4 to compensate. Raising ScaledNormalStepSolver.max_iter to 500 does not help (DUALC2/5/8 trust_region_collapse at feas 0.84-0.92, DUALC1 max_steps). The projector inexactness (m=278 > 100 CG iterations) is real but secondary (g1-projector-cg-budget). Needs row scaling / equilibration of the constraint rows in the normal-step least squares (a design change in the scaled subproblem), not a one-line fix. No branch.
